title: Runtime precision orchestrator with calibration pipeline integration
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We currently choose kernels at a coarse granularity (model-wide or static per-deployment) which leads to suboptimal latency/cost trade-offs and occasional accuracy regressions when deploying INT8/FP8 profiles alongside FP16. Goal: Implement a runtime "precision orchestrator" that uses per-request and per-layer quantization profiles (FP16/FP8/INT8) produced by the calibration pipeline to select the optimal kernel implementation at dispatch time. The orchestrator must be pipeline-aware (understand KV-cache effects and prefix reuse), respect SLOs, and enforce an accuracy gate backed by validation suites. Scope: - Integrate with existing calibration artifacts (per-op scale/zero-point, per-layer dynamic ranges, profile confidence scores). - Implement a lightweight runtime policy engine that selects kernels per-op or per-block, with fast fallback to higher-precision paths on accuracy or safety triggers. - Add telemetry to measure policy decisions, per-token latency/cost, and accuracy deltas vs. FP16 baseline. Out of scope: model re-training and offline profile generation (except as inputs).
acceptance_criteria: Precision orchestrator is integrated into the serving runtime and selectable via model config
Per-layer kernel selection latency overhead < 1.5ms for typical generation requests (seq_len=128)
End-to-end average token cost reduction >= 18% on mixed workloads vs FP16 baseline for target models
Accuracy regression relative to calibrated validation set <= 0.5% for top-1 token match and <= 0.75% for LM perplexity on benchmark prompts
Automated safety fallback triggers (quality gate) that revert to FP16 for anomalous distributions
Dashboard shows per-request decision traces and aggregate policy metrics
E2E canary rollout with canary and shadowing enabled; rollback in < 30 minutes if threshold breached
implementation_notes: Design a tiny rule engine with prioritized policies: 1) profile confidence threshold (from calibration), 2) runtime latency budget, 3) historical accuracy penalty for a model+prompt bucket. Store per-model profiles as immutable artifacts referenced by model-version. Kernel descriptors will include supported precisions and an expected accuracy loss estimate from offline calibration. At dispatch, prefer lowest-cost kernel that meets current policy. Use fast path caching of decisions for repeated prefix keys to avoid repeated policy evals.
calibration_workflow: Consume calibration outputs: per-op scales, quantization histograms, and profile confidence scores
Compute expected accuracy deltas per-op and aggregate a per-layer/segment risk score
Produce a 'profile manifest' that includes candidate precision for each op, fallback precision, and recommended kernel ids
Attach validation artifacts: small set of representative prompts, golden outputs, and numeric tolerances
Publish profile manifest to model artifact store and surface it to runtime via model metadata
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy engine decision matrix and fallback logic
Microbenchmarks: dispatch latency, decision cache hit rate, kv-cache interaction cases
Regression suite against calibrated validation prompts measuring top-1/token match and perplexity
A/B canary: 5% production traffic with shadowing to compare outputs and metrics
Chaos tests: simulate kernel failures and ensure graceful fallback without request loss
rollout_steps: Stage 1: Feature flag gated deploy to staging with sample models and synthetic load
Stage 2: Canary deploy to 5% of traffic for non-critical tenants with shadowing enabled
Stage 3: Monitor accuracy and latency metrics for 48h; run automated canary checks
Stage 4: Progressive ramp to 50% then 100% with rollback criteria enforced
Post-rollout: 2-week observability retention increase for decision traces
risks: Undetected accuracy regressions for tail prompts - mitigated by conservative profile thresholds and expanded validation set
Performance regressions due to per-op decision overhead - mitigated by decision caching and hot-path optimizations
Complexity in debugging multi-precision traces - mitigate with structured traces and trace-to-request linking
Interference with KV cache semantics if kernel fallback alters tokenization or hidden-state layout - require strict compatibility tests
